3. After service of summons, the defendant Nos.1 to 4 appeared through their counsel and filed common written statement denying the case of the plaintiff.
Relationship among the parties is not in dispute.

It is contended that, the plaintiff is not in joint possession of the suit schedule properties;
hence, the Court fee paid by the plaintiff is not proper.
The suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Father of the plaintiff by name Sri.Ramanand and his sons i.e., plaintiff and defendant Nos.3 & 4 were the members of the joint family.
After coming into existence of registered release deed dated 02.05.2005, the status of the joint family was dissolved and disintegrated and ceases to exist.
Sri. Ramanand

Sri. Ramanand

Sri.Ramanand engaged about 100 workers for the centering work of Maruthi Constructions.
Sri.Ramanand alone invested his money for commencing the business.
Sri . Ramanand invested huge amount of money and made huge earnings and substantial profits out of the Maruthi Constructions.
Sri.Ramanand with a zeal to acquire properties, invested, pooled and chanalised the aforementioned funds, money and amounts emanating from the said headings in acquiring the suit schedule properties.

In view of these two release deeds dated 02/05/2005 and 2/2/2011 and after taking property, the plaintiff has sold the same, which shows that, he has acted upon the release deeds.
Hence, the plaintiff has no right to claim partition again in respect of the suit schedule properties.
After release deeds, the plaintiff has made a departure from the joint family, there is no re-entry and there is no re-joining the family and the plaintiff is residing separately.

The plaintiff has voluntarily walked away from the joint family by taking his share, now,

The plaintiff after executing two release deeds, having taken away certain properties with all clarity sense of definiteness, certainty and unambiguously in a crystal clear manner has unequivocally stated that, the plaintiff released all his right, title and interest in the properties both immovable and movable, which are the suit schedule properties in favour of defendants and the plaintiff is disentitle to seek partition.

sentences.text: Wife of the plaintiff examined as PW.2 and deposed in support of the case of her husband.
PW.2 in her cross- examination has stated that, on 26.07.2013, her husband purchased site measuring 30 x 40 feet in the name of this plaintiff and his wife / PW.2.
Admittedly, the plaintiff demanded his share in the joint family properties in the year 2005.
There was also quarrel between the plaintiff and his father.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.25, release deed came into existence or has been executed by the plaintiff by receiving properties of his share as mentioned therein.

In the said registered release deed, the plaintiff has clearly stated that, after receiving the properties mentioned in the release deed Ex.P.25, he will not claim any share in the remaining properties of the defendants.

The plaintiff has took the property given to him under the release deed Ex.P.25 and he has got the same mutated in his name and he has alienated the said property, now, the plaintiff is not challenging the release deed and the plaintiff has not included the properties given to him under the release deed and the plaintiff has filed this suit for partition stating that, no partition has taken place.

By the conduct of the plaintiff, he is estopped from claiming partition as already he has taken properties of his share, hence, as on the date of the suit, the suit schedule properties were not the joint family properties of plaintiff and defendants.

Further, the plaintiff has executed the registered release deeds as per Ex.P.25 and Ex.P.27 and acted upon them i.e., by taking properties, he has alienated the same, which amounts to acting upon the release deed.

Under such circumstances,
it cannot be held that, the plaintiff remained in joint possession and joint family, as there is no any evidence that, there was a joint or reconstituting of joint family.

As discussed above, plaintiff has voluntarily executed the release deeds and taken properties towards his share, hence, Ex.P.25 and Ex.P.27 release deeds cannot be considered as they are outcome of threat, inducement, misrepresentation etc., as the said release deeds are not challenged by the plaintiff stating that, they are not binding on him etc.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 and addl. issue Nos.1 & 2 are in the Negative and issue No.3 is in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.2:

Defendants in their written statement have simply contended that,
the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

In the written statement, the defendants have not stated the names of persons, who required to be added as parties in this suit, but the defendants have simply stated that, the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Based on that assertion, the Court has framed this issue No.2.
However, in the cross-examination of PW.1, the defendants' counsel has cross-examined that, the plaintiff has not arrayed the brother and sister of father of the plaintiff i.e., V.Ramanand.
In this case, there is no dispute regarding the properties between the father of the plaintiff and his brothers i.e., brothers of Sri.V.Ramanand.

Hence, the suit filed against the defendants, who are mother, sister and brothers of this plaintiff, are the necessary parties and there are no other persons required to be added as parties to this suit.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the Negative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff filed this suit for partition seeking his 1/5 th share in the suit schedule properties.
Father of the plaintiff intended to deny the lawful share of plaintiff in the joint family properties.
Hence, in the year 2005, plaintiff's father represented to the plaintiff that, he would give plaintiff's legitimate share in the joint family properties subject to condition that, the plaintiff has to execute a registered release deed.
At the relevant point of time, the plaintiff requested his father to partition family properties and to execute registered partition deed by allotting separate shares to each individual members of the family.
Plaintiff was unaware of the said agreements till the agreement holder G.Giriyappa instituted original suits seeking the relief of specific performance, which indicate that, plaintiff's father has mislead plaintiff by his false representations and made him to execute registered release deed.
In the mean time,
plaintiff had sustained bullet injury and was not in position to earn his livelihood and maintain his family.
Accordingly, plaintiff's father executed a registered gift deed dated 02.02.2011 in favour of plaintiff's minor children in respect of house bearing No.10, Thimmaiah Garden Main Road,
Corporation Division 46, Bengaluru.
Thereafter, plaintiff's father threatened and demanded the plaintiff to execute a release deed.
Under such circumstances, on 02.02.2011, the plaintiff executed the registered release deed.
In the said release deeds, it is indicated that, in view of execution of the said documents, plaintiffs and his wife and children do not have any manner of right over self-acquired properties of plaintiff's father.
The suit schedule properties are the ancestral and joint family properties.
Hence, release deeds dated 02.05.2005 and 02.02.2011 do not take away the plaintiffs' right in the suit schedule properties.
Defendants refused to effect partition stating that, plaintiff has already executed release deed and thereby denied to allot plaintiff's lawful share in the schedule properties.
Hence, the plaintiff has filed this suit seeking 1/5 th share in the suit schedule properties.
3. After service of summons, the defendant Nos.1 to 4 appeared through their counsel and filed common written statement denying the case of the plaintiff.
It is contended that, the plaintiff is not in joint possession of the suit schedule properties;
hence, the Court fee paid by the plaintiff is not proper.
The suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
After coming into existence of registered release deed dated 02.05.2005, the status of the joint family was dissolved and disintegrated and ceases to exist.
was the sole proprietor of M/s.Maruthi Constructions.
was involved, immersed in the centering work for the past 40 years.
Sri.Ramanand engaged about 100 workers for the centering work of Maruthi Constructions.
Sri.Ramanand alone invested his money for commencing the business.
Sri . Ramanand invested huge amount of money and made huge earnings and substantial profits out of the Maruthi Constructions.
Sri.Ramanand with a zeal to acquire properties, invested, pooled and chanalised the aforementioned funds, money and amounts emanating from the said headings in acquiring the suit schedule properties.
3a) Suit schedule 'A' and 'B' properties were given to the share of Sri.Ramanand under the family partition dated 18.11.1997.
The suit schedule 'A' and 'B' properties were never constituted ancestral and joint family nucleus for acquiring the aforementioned suit schedule properties.
Thus, remaining properties were the self-acquired properties of Sri.Ramanand.
3b) Suit Schedule C property was purchased by Sri.Ramanand out of his earnings under the registered Sale Deed dated 04.05.2005.
Hence, it is the self-acquired property of Sri.Ramanand.
Sri.Ramanand during his life time got the said properties mutated into his name and he was in possession and enjoyment of the same.
Sri.Ramanand alone had executed lease deeds and he alone was collecting the rents from the tenants and he was paying huge taxes to the concerned authorities.
Hence, suit schedule M property is the self-acquired property of defendant No.4 and defendant No.4 is recovering the rents in respect of the said property from the tenants.
Hence, the said properties are the self acquired property of Sri.Ramanand.
Thereafter, said suit schedule Q property was acquired by KIADB and possession of the said land was taken from Sri.Ramanand and defendant No.4 taking the note of their joint ownership rights and possession, compensation was awarded to defendant No.1 since Sri.Ramanand was dead at that point of time.
In pursuance of the release deed, the plaintiff obtained RTC, mutation and paid land revenue and exercised his ownership right and possession in respect of said 5 Acres 29 guntas of land.
Apart from this land measuring 2 Acres 11 guntas in Sy.No.1, which was sold out under the said sale deed was never the absolute property of the plaintiff and this extent of land was not even shown in the suit schedule.
After existence of this release deed, the plaintiff sold away the said 5 Acre 29 guntas of land along with the lands measuring 2 Acres 11 guntas in Sy. No.1 of Kenchanahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk under the registered sale deed dated 26.10.2005 for heavy sale price of Rs.1,00,00,000/- and the plaintiff utilized the said sale price for his own use and for purchasing of other properties.
Plaintiff also purchased other landed properties in and around Bengaluru out of the sale price of the property obtained by the plaintiff under the release deed.
Plaintiff earned and made huge chunk of money.
Hence, the plaintiff has no right to claim partition again in respect of the suit schedule properties.
After release deeds, the plaintiff has made a departure from the joint family, there is no re-entry and there is no re-joining the family and the plaintiff is residing separately.
The plaintiff has voluntarily walked away from the joint family by taking his share, now,
he is estopped from claiming the relief of partition.
The plaintiff after executing two release deeds, having taken away certain properties with all clarity sense of definiteness, certainty and unambiguously in a crystal clear manner has unequivocally stated that, the plaintiff released all his right, title and interest in the properties both immovable and movable, which are the suit schedule properties in favour of defendants and the plaintiff is disentitle to seek partition.
